articleBody: Window replacement or installation can affect energy performance, weather resistance, security, and code compliance, so it is not just a finish upgrade. The U.S. Department of Energy explains that properly selected and installed windows can reduce heat gain, heat loss, and HVAC loads, especially when the product matches the climate and orientation. In California, replacement windows also need to comply with energy standards and often involve installation details that support air sealing and proper flashing. For Los Angeles County projects, the contractor should explain whether the windows are replacement units, retrofit inserts, or full-frame replacements, because each approach has different impacts on trim, siding, insulation, and structural openings. Buyers should ask about glazing type, U-factor, solar heat gain coefficient, and whether the windows meet safety requirements for locations near floors, stairs, or showers. Installation quality is critical: even a high-quality window will underperform if flashing, sealing, or sill preparation is poor. Homeowners should also consider lead safety in older buildings and whether the installation will disturb surrounding finishes. If the project is part of a larger remodel, window work should be sequenced before interior finishes to avoid damage and rework. A strong contractor will provide manufacturer specs, explain warranty conditions, and confirm how the new units integrate with insulation and waterproofing.
